heroHeadline: Warsh Senate Cloture Vote at 5:30 PM ET Today; Bessent-He Seoul Trade Talks Confirmed May 12-13; April CPI Tomorrow; Oil Bounces to $104 Brent as Iran Ceasefire Stalls
heroSubtitle: May 11: The most consequential macro week of 2026 is underway. Warsh Senate cloture vote at 5:30 PM ET (92% confirmation probability; first FOMC as Chair June 9-10); Powell expires May 15 (4 days). Pre-summit Bessent-He Lifeng trade talks confirmed Seoul May 12-13 before Trump-Xi Beijing summit (May 14-15) — 'Board of Trade' proposal signals shift to managed trade; Iran agenda may crowd out tariff de-escalation from the elevated bilateral barrier. S&P 500 ~7,399 (six-week winning streak; Times of Israel: 'record highs on US-Iran peace deal hopes') but oil bounced sharply: Brent +2.7% to $104/WTI +2.7% to $98 on May 10-11 as Fortune reported 'ceasefire plans going nowhere' and Iran's 14-point MOU remains under Khamenei review. RSM cut US 2026 GDP forecast to 1.7% (stagflation lite scenario). April CPI (due May 12) is the week's critical inflation test — March CPI was 3.3% (gas +21.2% YoY); a hot April print would cement the Warsh-era no-cut posture. Recession probabilities: Goldman ~20%, JPMorgan ~25%, Moody's ~40% — all predicated on continued ceasefire progress that is not materializing. Core PCE 3.2% (hottest since Iran war began), ISM Services Prices Paid 70.7 (highest since 2022), Section 122 tariff cliff July 23 (73 days; no Congressional extension bill) — the Warsh era begins with a complex, stagflationary inheritance.
